speaker: interviewer
text: Hi Tomasz, thanks for joining. How's your day going?

speaker: interviewee
text: Busy, but fine. I've got a call at the top of the hour, so we're good till then.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, it shouldn't take more than twenty minutes. No wrong answers, just your experience.

speaker: interviewee
text: Sure, go ahead.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Tell me a bit about your household and who does the food shopping.

speaker: interviewee
text: It's me and my wife Ana, and her brother is staying with us for a while. I do most of the cooking, so I do most of the shopping. Weekends we used to go to the market by the old station.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. And how did you hear about Shmuber Eats?

speaker: interviewee
text: An ad on a podcast, I think. One of those read-out ads in the middle.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. Walk me through your last order, from opening the app to putting things away.

speaker: interviewee
text: Okay. So this was the week we got the keys to the new flat, boxes up to the ceiling, I had no idea where the nearest shop even was, and our car was still parked at Ana's parents'. So I ordered the basics and some things to cook properly. Pasta, tomatoes, cheese, and flour, because I wanted to make pizza on the first night, it's a little tradition of ours. Now we've unpacked, I know there's a really decent market ten minutes' walk away, so that's where I go.

speaker: interviewer
text: Okay. Let's move on. How often do you order groceries online?

speaker: interviewee
text: That was the one time, really. I opened the app again once but I didn't order.

speaker: interviewer
text: And when you opened it again, what were you looking for?

speaker: interviewee
text: A particular sausage, the smoked one from home. They didn't have it.

speaker: interviewer
text: Got it. Tell me about the last time an item in your order was substituted.

speaker: interviewee
text: The tomatoes were a different brand, that's fine. The cheese came as two small packs instead of one big one. Also fine.

speaker: interviewer
text: Did you get a message about those before the delivery?

speaker: interviewee
text: Maybe? I was busy all afternoon, I didn't look at my phone. I saw it on the receipt.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. How do you keep track of what you need between orders?

speaker: interviewee
text: Ana has a list app, I just look at the fridge. Her brother doesn't buy food, he just eats it.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Does anyone else add to Ana's list?

speaker: interviewee
text: I do, sometimes, when she reminds me to. Mostly it's hers.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. How did you pick the delivery window last time?

speaker: interviewee
text: I took six to eight, because I knew we'd be home. It came right at the start, six ten or so.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. What would you think of a monthly delivery pass, and what would you pay for it?

speaker: interviewee
text: For us, no. I like to choose my own things in the market. If I ordered every week, maybe five, six.

speaker: interviewer
text: And what would make a pass worth it for you?

speaker: interviewee
text: If it was cheaper than the bus fare to the big supermarket, I suppose. But I don't take the bus there anyway.

speaker: interviewer
text: Okay. Great. What did you like most about the order?

speaker: interviewee
text: The driver was friendly, and it was on time.

speaker: interviewer
text: And what did you like least?

speaker: interviewee
text: The flour. I'd asked for strong bread flour for the pizza dough, and they swapped it for a bag of self-raising cake flour, which, for pizza, it puffs up like a sponge.

speaker: interviewer
text: Oh no. Self-raising for pizza dough? What happened with the pizza?

speaker: interviewee
text: It was like a focaccia that had a bad day. We ate it, we laughed, but it wasn't pizza.

speaker: interviewer
text: Did the picker get in touch about that one, or was it just in the bag?

speaker: interviewee
text: Just in the bag. Same word, flour, so I guess on the screen it looked like a match.

speaker: interviewer
text: Got it, that's really helpful, thank you. Great. On a scale of one to ten, how was it overall?

speaker: interviewee
text: Six. Fine, but not special.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Would you recommend Shmuber Eats to a friend?

speaker: interviewee
text: Maybe to someone who doesn't cook much. For a cook, the swaps are a risk.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. Last question, is there anything about your orders I didn't ask about?

speaker: interviewee
text: No, I think we covered it. Good luck with it.

speaker: interviewer
text: Thank you so much Tomasz, really appreciate your time.

speaker: interviewee
text: No problem. Bye.
